nominations.contribution: for their analysis of corporate governance and the mechanisms of investor protection

nominations.rationale: Their foundational work on corporate governance bridged legal institutions, agency theory, and firm performance. They identified the crucial mechanisms through which investor protection and control rights shape capital allocation and real economic outcomes.

nominations.contribution: for their development of empirical methods for demand estimation and market structure analysis
key_works: Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They pioneered the use of structural empirical methods to test theories of market structure and firm behavior against granular microdata. Their framework provides the rigorous mechanism-based analysis necessary to evaluate the real effects of market power and regulation.

nominations.contribution: for her empirical research on corporate governance, family firms, and organizational economics
key_works: Bertrand and Schoar, 2003: Managing with Style: The Effect of Managers on Firm Policies, The Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Her innovative use of microdata to analyze family firms, executive incentives, and governance structures has consistently identified the precise frictions in organizational design. She rigorously separates the real effects of managerial characteristics from endogenous selection.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of firm dynamics and job creation and destruction
key_works: Davis and Haltiwanger, 1992: Gross Job Creation, Gross Job Destruction, and Employment Reallocation, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: They pioneered the use of longitudinal administrative firm registers to unpack aggregate employment changes into micro-level dynamics. This granular focus on selection, mismatch, and reallocation fundamentally changed labor and business economics.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of management practices and firm productivity
key_works: Bloom and Van Reenen, 2007: Measuring and Explaining Management Practices Across Firms and Countries, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Their innovative data-collection and quasi-experimental designs provided the first large-scale credible evidence on how organizational inputs shape productivity. They effectively treat firm management as an endogenous human capital input with long-run effects.

nominations.contribution: for structural empirical methods to estimate market power and product differentiation
key_works: Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They developed the workhorse structural framework for identifying demand and substitution patterns from observational data. This methodology tightly links microeconomic theory with empirical estimation to allow for credible counterfactual policy analysis.

nominations.contribution: for empirical methods in the analysis of collusive behavior and market competition
key_works: Porter, 1983: A Study of Cartel Stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Their pioneering empirical IO work showed how to credibly identify unobserved firm behavior and market power from aggregate data. It provided a new paradigm for bridging oligopoly theory with the statistical evaluation of antitrust policy.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of sunk costs and the evolution of market structure
key_works: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure: Price Competition, Advertising, and the Evolution of Concentration, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: He advanced the theory of industrial organization by linking endogenous investments to long-run market concentration. His theoretical bounds approach is highly robust and maps beautifully to historical and empirical evidence on industry dynamics.

nominations.contribution: for their structural empirical framework for modeling market demand and equilibrium in differentiated product markets
nominations.rationale: Their structural empirical framework for modeling demand and market power has become an indispensable tool. It allows researchers to rigorously evaluate the causal impacts of regulations and institutional shifts in differentiated markets.

nominations.contribution: for their empirical measurement of management practices and their causal impact on firm productivity
nominations.rationale: By undertaking systematic, large-scale empirical data collection across countries, they provided credible evidence that variations in management practices causally explain substantial differences in firm productivity.

nominations.contribution: for their empirical analysis of media markets, ideological segregation, and political economy
nominations.rationale: Their exceptionally creative use of novel data sources and rigorous design-based empirical strategies has illuminated the functioning of media markets, ideological segregation, and their political economy impacts.

nominations.contribution: for his introduction of dynamic structural estimation methods to the empirical analysis of business decisions
nominations.rationale: His pioneering introduction of dynamic structural estimation methods enables researchers to formally model and uncover the unobserved incentives and institutional constraints driving long-run business decisions.

nominations.contribution: for their empirical analysis of selection and moral hazard in insurance markets
nominations.rationale: Their compelling use of administrative data to identify selection and moral hazard in health insurance markets demonstrates exactly how institutional design impacts market viability and social welfare.

nominations.contribution: for their development of empirical methods for structural demand estimation and market equilibrium
key_works: Berry, Levinsohn & Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: The BLP framework revolutionized empirical IO by allowing for realistic substitution patterns and unobserved product characteristics in differentiated markets. This is the cornerstone for modern analysis of competition, consumer choices, and merger remedies.

nominations.contribution: for his empirical research on industrial organization, pricing, and merger analysis
key_works: Nevo, 2001: Measuring Market Power in the Ready-to-Eat Cereal Industry, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Nevo's structural estimation of demand and supply in retail markets provides highly credible evidence on market power and price dynamics. His work directly informs competition enforcement and our understanding of consumer behavior in product markets.

nominations.contribution: for his analysis of market structure, endogenous sunk costs, and industrial concentration
key_works: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure: Price Competition, Advertising, and the Evolution of Concentration, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Sutton's integration of game-theoretic models with robust empirical bounds fundamentally improved how economists view market structure. His insights into how firm investments shape competition remain essential for understanding concentrated markets.

nominations.contribution: for his pioneering development of structural estimation methods for dynamic discrete choice models
key_works: Rust, 1987: Optimal Replacement of GMC Bus Engines: An Empirical Model of Harold Zurcher, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: Rust's methodology enabled researchers to empirically model the forward-looking decisions of firms and consumers under uncertainty. This provided a rigorous micro-foundation for evaluating long-term strategic behavior and equipment replacement.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to the economics of antitrust and competition policy
key_works: Whinston, 1990: Tying, Foreclosure, and Exclusion, American Economic Review
Shapiro, 1989: Theories of Oligopoly Behavior, Handbook of Industrial Organization
nominations.rationale: Their rigorous application of microeconomic theory to antitrust questions has reshaped both academic research and practical competition enforcement. They have clarified the precise mechanisms through which mergers and vertical restraints impact market outcomes.

nominations.contribution: for their development of structural econometric methods to estimate demand and model market equilibrium
key_works: Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: They developed a structural, tractable methodology allowing complex, unobserved consumer heterogeneity to aggregate efficiently into market demand. This computationally innovative framework permanently elevated quantitative market analysis.

nominations.contribution: for the measurement of management practices and their causal impact on firm productivity
key_works: Bloom and Van Reenen, 2007: Measuring and Explaining Management Practices Across Firms and Countries, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: They constructed systematic, long-run firm-level datasets to correct missing components of productivity growth. Their work disciplines macroeconomic models by unearthing tangible sources of total factor productivity differences.

nominations.contribution: for structural models of firm-level innovation and the macroeconomic productivity slowdown
key_works: Akcigit and Kerr, 2018: Growth through Heterogeneous Innovations, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: He constructed quantitative frameworks linking micro-level firm dynamics and patenting behavior to aggregate productivity trends. It successfully addresses long-standing puzzles about missing growth in general equilibrium.

nominations.contribution: for his theory of market structure, endogenous sunk costs, and market concentration
key_works: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: He derived robust theoretical bounds on market structure that remain stable across alternative specifications. His work showed how fundamental microeconomic technologies shape long-run industrial concentration.

nominations.contribution: for their pioneering contributions to the empirical modeling of market power and collusion
key_works: Porter, 1983: A Study of Cartel Stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: They formulated disciplined structural models that permit the identification of unobservable anti-competitive behavior from aggregate market data, demonstrating how rigorous micro-foundations yield testable macro-level implications.

nominations.contribution: for their development of empirical methods for analyzing market power and consumer welfare
key_works: Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: By providing a tractable method to estimate demand in differentiated product markets, Berry and Pakes enable the rigorous quantification of welfare and efficiency trade-offs in applied market settings.

nominations.contribution: for her contributions to the industrial organization of internet search and platform markets
key_works: Athey and Ellison, 2011: Position Auctions with Consumer Search, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: Athey's formal modeling of platform economics directly applies mechanism design logic to new matching environments, improving real-world allocation systems with rigorous theory.

nominations.contribution: for their contributions to the theory of the firm and the economics of contracts
key_works: Bolton and Dewatripont, 2005: Contract Theory, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Their extensive work on contract theory maps directly to the design of robust organizational incentives and the boundaries of efficient allocation under asymmetric information.

nominations.contribution: for their analysis of network effects and competition policy
key_works: Katz and Shapiro, 1985: Network Externalities, Competition, and Compatibility, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: They provided the foundational formal analysis of markets where consumption choices are interlinked, deeply informing subsequent regulatory and market design policy.

nominations.contribution: for his theoretical and empirical analysis of market structure and the evolution of industries
key_works: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: Sutton establishes strict theoretical bounds on market concentration derived from basic primitives of competition, a methodologically clean approach that yields robust, generalizable principles.

nominations.contribution: for the structural empirical analysis of differentiated-products demand and market power
key_works: Berry, 1994: Estimating discrete-choice models of product differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile prices in market equilibrium, Econometrica
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 2004: Differentiated products demand systems from a combination of micro and macro data, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: The BLP framework created a replicable template for measuring demand, markups, mergers and welfare in real markets. Its assumptions are contestable, but the field has made unusually transparent progress by stress-testing instruments, substitution patterns and counterfactuals.

nominations.contribution: for methods to estimate productivity, firm dynamics and the effects of market selection
key_works: Olley and Pakes, 1996: The dynamics of productivity in the telecommunications equipment industry, Econometrica
Levinsohn and Petrin, 2003: Estimating production functions using inputs to control for unobservables, Review of Economic Studies
Petrin and Levinsohn, 2012: Measuring aggregate productivity growth using plant-level data, RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This work improved a core measurement problem: separating true productivity from selection, investment and input choices. The methods have been replicated and criticized across many industries, which has clarified rather than weakened their scientific value.

nominations.contribution: for the new empirical industrial organization and the measurement of oligopoly conduct
key_works: Bresnahan, 1982: The oligopoly solution concept is identified, Economics Letters
Bresnahan, 1989: Empirical studies of industries with market power, Handbook of Industrial Organization
Bresnahan and Reiss, 1991: Entry and competition in concentrated markets, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Bresnahan’s work made market-power hypotheses operational and falsifiable with industry data. From a credibility standpoint, its importance lies in shifting IO toward explicit models that could be rejected by evidence.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of two-sided markets, platforms and indirect network effects

people.name: Jean-Charles Rochet

Armstrong, 2006: Competition in two-sided markets, RAND Journal of Economics
Rochet and Tirole, 2006: Two-sided markets: a progress report, RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The contribution gave economists a language for platform pricing, participation externalities and regulation that is now indispensable. The empirical literature is younger and less settled, so I would rank it below the most mature IO measurement contributions.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical and policy analysis of electricity markets and regulated network industries

nominations.rationale: This line of work combines theory, institutional detail and market data in a way that directly affected regulation. The evidence is context-specific, but that specificity is a strength when evaluating actual policy design.

nominations.contribution: for empirical methods to estimate demand, market power and product differentiation
key_works: Berry, 1994: Estimating Discrete-Choice Models of Product Differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
Pakes, 2003: A Reconsideration of Hedonic Price Indexes with an Application to PC's, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This contribution turned industrial organization into a quantitatively credible empirical field. Its strength, from my perspective, is the explicit attention to identification, measurement and counterfactual policy relevance.

nominations.contribution: for empirical analysis of entry, competition and market structure
key_works: Bresnahan and Reiss, 1991: Entry and Competition in Concentrated Markets, Journal of Political Economy
Bresnahan and Reiss, 1990: Entry in Monopoly Markets, Review of Economic Studies
nominations.rationale: Their work made the number of firms and market-entry patterns informative about competitive conduct. I value its transparent use of observable institutional and market thresholds to infer otherwise hidden economic behavior.

nominations.contribution: for the economics of two-sided markets and platform competition
key_works: Rochet and Tirole, 2003: Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets, Journal of the European Economic Association
Armstrong, 2006: Competition in Two-Sided Markets, RAND Journal of Economics
Rochet and Tirole, 2006: Two-Sided Markets: A Progress Report, RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The contribution clarified why pricing, access and regulation differ when platforms coordinate distinct user groups. It has large policy value, though institutional details of governance and enforcement are crucial in applying the theory.

nominations.contribution: for methods to measure firm productivity, selection and reallocation
key_works: Olley and Pakes, 1996: The Dynamics of Productivity in the Telecommunications Equipment Industry, Econometrica
Levinsohn and Petrin, 2003: Estimating Production Functions Using Inputs to Control for Unobservables, Review of Economic Studies
nominations.rationale: This work created tools for measuring productivity dynamics inside industries, rather than assuming them away. For a committee concerned with state capacity and regulation, reliable measurement of firm performance and reallocation is indispensable.

nominations.contribution: for the evolutionary theory of firm routines and industrial dynamics
key_works: Nelson and Winter, 1982: An Evolutionary Theory of Economic Change, Harvard University Press
Winter, 1964: Economic Natural Selection and the Theory of the Firm, Yale Economic Essays
nominations.rationale: The contribution offered a durable alternative to purely optimizing models of the firm by emphasizing routines, learning and selection. It has influenced economics, management and institutional analysis, even if its empirical operationalization is less unified than in modern IO.

nominations.contribution: for methods for estimating demand and market power in differentiated-product industries
key_works: Berry, 1994: "Estimating Discrete-Choice Models of Product Differentiation", RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: "Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium", Econometrica
Nevo, 2001: "Measuring Market Power in the Ready-to-Eat Cereal Industry", Econometrica
nominations.rationale: BLP made structural empirical industrial organization a quantitative general-equilibrium tool for market-power, merger and product-policy counterfactuals. The core contribution is clearly attributable and remains the workhorse of modern IO.

nominations.contribution: for methods for measuring firm productivity and the dynamics of production
key_works: Olley and Pakes, 1996: "The Dynamics of Productivity in the Telecommunications Equipment Industry", Econometrica
Levinsohn and Petrin, 2003: "Estimating Production Functions Using Inputs to Control for Unobservables", Review of Economic Studies
Ackerberg, Caves and Frazer, 2015: "Identification Properties of Recent Production Function Estimators", Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This work gave empirical content to productivity, reallocation and firm dynamics, central objects for both IO and macro. Its value lies in a disciplined bridge from micro production decisions to aggregate efficiency.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of two-sided markets and platform competition
key_works: Rochet and Tirole, 2003: "Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets", Journal of the European Economic Association
Armstrong, 2006: "Competition in Two-Sided Markets", RAND Journal of Economics
Caillaud and Jullien, 2003: "Chicken and Egg: Competition among Intermediation Service Providers", RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The contribution clarified pricing and welfare when participation externalities connect distinct user groups. Its policy influence is large in digital-market regulation, though attribution is shared with a broad literature.

nominations.contribution: for dynamic models of firm and industry evolution
key_works: Hopenhayn, 1992: "Entry, Exit, and Firm Dynamics in Long Run Equilibrium", Econometrica
Ericson and Pakes, 1995: "Markov-Perfect Industry Dynamics: A Framework for Empirical Work", Review of Economic Studies
Pakes and McGuire, 1994: "Computing Markov-Perfect Nash Equilibria: Numerical Implications of a Dynamic Differentiated Product Model", RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: These models made entry, exit, productivity and strategic investment analyzable in dynamic equilibrium. The framework is attractive from my lens because it turns industry structure into an endogenous long-run outcome.

nominations.contribution: for the real-options analysis of irreversible investment and firm decision-making under uncertainty
key_works: McDonald and Siegel, 1986: "The Value of Waiting to Invest", Quarterly Journal of Economics
Pindyck, 1991: "Irreversibility, Uncertainty, and Investment", Journal of Economic Literature
Dixit and Pindyck, 1994: Investment under Uncertainty, Princeton University Press
nominations.rationale: The real-options approach gave a simple dynamic logic for why uncertainty and irreversibility reshape investment timing. Its core mechanism is robust and has influenced production, energy and regulatory economics.

nominations.contribution: for the development of structural empirical methods for measuring demand, market power and welfare in differentiated-product markets
key_works: Berry, 1994: Estimating discrete-choice models of product differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile prices in market equilibrium, Econometrica
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 2004: Differentiated products demand systems from a combination of micro and macro data, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This contribution transformed industrial organization into a quantitatively credible empirical field with tools now used in competition policy worldwide. I value its combination of explicit economic structure, careful measurement and counterfactual welfare analysis.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of productivity differences, reallocation and resource misallocation across firms

nominations.rationale: Sutton gave the field robust equilibrium restrictions linking technology, advertising, R&D and concentration. The work is valuable because it provides mechanisms that survive beyond particular institutional details.

nominations.rationale: BLP is a paradigmatic case of theory-guided empirics opening an institutional black box: pricing, substitution and market power inside oligopolies. It created durable tools for policy practice in antitrust and regulation.

key_works: Bresnahan, 1982: The Oligopoly Solution Concept Is Identified, Economics Letters
Porter, 1983: A Study of Cartel Stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics
Bresnahan and Reiss, 1991: Entry and Competition in Concentrated Markets, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: Their work made market power and collusion measurable rather than merely theoretical. The institutional detail in the historical and industry settings is a major strength, though extrapolation across markets must be handled cautiously.

nominations.contribution: for the economic analysis of management practices and productivity differences across firms

people.name: John Van Reenen
people.affiliation: London School of Economics and Massachusetts Institute of Technology

key_works: Bloom and Van Reenen, 2007: Measuring and Explaining Management Practices across Firms and Countries, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Bloom, Eifert, Mahajan, McKenzie and Roberts, 2013: Does Management Matter? Evidence from India, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Bloom, Sadun and Van Reenen, 2012: Americans Do IT Better: US Multinationals and the Productivity Miracle, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This body of work opened the black box of the firm using new data and, in some cases, experimental evidence. It fits my evidentiary preferences because it connects institutional organization inside firms to measured productivity and inequality across workplaces.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of two-sided markets and platform competition
key_works: Rochet and Tirole, 2003: Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets, Journal of the European Economic Association
Armstrong, 2006: Competition in Two-Sided Markets, RAND Journal of Economics
Rochet and Tirole, 2006: Two-Sided Markets: A Progress Report, RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The theory of platforms has become central for competition policy in digital and payment markets. I would support it for clarifying mechanisms of pricing and participation, while noting that empirical identification of platform harms and benefits remains demanding.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm capabilities, appropriability and innovation strategy
key_works: Teece, 1986: Profiting from Technological Innovation, Research Policy
Teece, Pisano and Shuen, 1997: Dynamic Capabilities and Strategic Management, Strategic Management Journal
Teece, 2010: Business Models, Business Strategy and Innovation, Long Range Planning
nominations.rationale: Teece’s work influenced how economists and business scholars think about why firms differ and how innovation rents are captured. I would rank it below the more tightly identified IO contributions, but it has had broad impact on the economics of organizations and strategy.

nominations.contribution: for developing structural empirical methods for estimating demand, market power and product differentiation
key_works: Berry, 1994: Estimating discrete-choice models of product differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile prices in market equilibrium, Econometrica
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 2004: Differentiated products demand systems from a combination of micro and macro data, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: This is the clearest IO candidate from an applied micro perspective: it changed how economists measure demand, markups, mergers and welfare in actual product markets. It links formal models to micro data at precisely the level where firms set prices and consumers choose.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of endogenous sunk costs, market structure and the limits of concentration

people.name: John Sutton
people.affiliation: London School of Economics and Political Science

key_works: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure, MIT Press
Sutton, 1998: Technology and Market Structure, MIT Press
Sutton, 2007: Market structure: Theory and evidence, Handbook of Industrial Organization
nominations.rationale: Sutton supplied a durable mechanism linking investment, advertising, R&D and concentration in ways that can be confronted with industry data. The work is especially valuable because it clarifies when larger markets increase competition and when they instead induce endogenous escalation.

nominations.contribution: for empirical models of entry, market structure and the measurement of competition
key_works: Bresnahan and Reiss, 1990: Entry in monopoly markets, Review of Economic Studies
Bresnahan and Reiss, 1991: Entry and competition in concentrated markets, Journal of Political Economy
Berry, 1992: Estimation of a model of entry in the airline industry, Econometrica
nominations.rationale: This contribution made entry decisions a practical source of evidence on competitive conduct. I would weigh it highly because it extracts market power from observed behavior in local markets rather than from accounting margins alone.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of network effects, compatibility, switching costs and strategic competition
key_works: Katz and Shapiro, 1985: Network externalities, competition, and compatibility, American Economic Review
Katz and Shapiro, 1986: Technology adoption in the presence of network externalities, Journal of Political Economy
Klemperer, 1987: Markets with consumer switching costs, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The work identified mechanisms now central to digital markets: installed bases, compatibility, lock-in and standards. It has clear policy relevance for competition enforcement, even if empirical implementation varies across markets.

nominations.contribution: for empirical methods to detect and measure collusion and market power in imperfectly competitive industries
key_works: Porter, 1983: A study of cartel stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics
Slade, 1987: Interfirm rivalry in a repeated game: An empirical test of tacit collusion, Journal of Industrial Economics
Ellison, 1994: Theories of cartel stability and the Joint Executive Committee, RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This line showed how dynamic pricing and conduct can reveal collusion using market-level evidence. It is less unified than BLP, but it speaks directly to enforcement and to the mechanisms through which firms sustain market power.

nominations.contribution: for the development of empirical methods for analyzing differentiated-product demand and market power
key_works: Berry, 1994: Estimating Discrete-Choice Models of Product Differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 2004: Differentiated Products Demand Systems from a Combination of Micro and Macro Data, Journal of Political Economy
nominations.rationale: BLP made the analysis of market power quantitative, structural and usable in real antitrust settings. Its importance is methodological and substantive: it turns firm-level and product-level data into disciplined equilibrium counterfactuals.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of endogenous sunk costs and the structure of industries
key_works: Sutton, 1991: Sunk Costs and Market Structure, MIT Press
Sutton, 1998: Technology and Market Structure, MIT Press
Sutton, 2007: Market Structure: Theory and Evidence, Handbook of Industrial Organization
nominations.rationale: Sutton supplied a parsimonious theory that explains robust cross-industry regularities in concentration, advertising and R&D. The work has exactly the virtue I value: a tractable mechanism with strong restrictions that can be confronted with data.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of management practices, productivity and firm performance
key_works: Bloom and Van Reenen, 2007: Measuring and Explaining Management Practices across Firms and Countries, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Bloom, Sadun and Van Reenen, 2012: Americans Do IT Better: US Multinationals and the Productivity Miracle, American Economic Review
Bloom, Eifert, Mahajan, McKenzie and Roberts, 2013: Does Management Matter? Evidence from India, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This research made a hard-to-measure component of productivity visible and comparable across firms and countries. It matters for aggregate growth because management quality provides a micro-founded source of persistent productivity differences.

nominations.contribution: for the analysis of firm dynamics, job creation and productivity reallocation

people.name: Steven J. Davis
people.affiliation: Hoover Institution and University of Chicago Booth School of Business

key_works: Davis and Haltiwanger, 1992: Gross Job Creation, Gross Job Destruction, and Employment Reallocation, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Davis, Haltiwanger and Schuh, 1996: Job Creation and Destruction, MIT Press
Haltiwanger, Jarmin and Miranda, 2013: Who Creates Jobs? Small versus Large versus Young, Review of Economics and Statistics
nominations.rationale: The contribution established firm turnover and reallocation as central facts for production and labor-market dynamics. It is highly valuable for macroeconomics because it links micro dispersion to aggregate productivity and employment movements.

nominations.contribution: for empirical methods to identify market power and conduct in oligopolistic industries
key_works: Bresnahan, 1982: The Oligopoly Solution Concept Is Identified, Economics Letters
Porter, 1983: A Study of Cartel Stability: The Joint Executive Committee, 1880-1886, Bell Journal of Economics
Bresnahan, 1989: Empirical Studies of Industries with Market Power, Handbook of Industrial Organization
nominations.rationale: This work moved industrial organization from descriptive concentration measures toward structural identification of conduct. It created tools for asking how much market outcomes reflect technology, demand or strategic behavior.

nominations.contribution: for empirical methods that identify demand, market power and welfare in differentiated-products industries
key_works: Berry, 1994: Estimating Discrete-Choice Models of Product Differentiation, RAND Journal of Economics
Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes, 1995: Automobile Prices in Market Equilibrium, Econometrica
Pakes, 2003: A Reconsideration of Hedonic Price Indexes with an Application to PCs, American Economic Review
nominations.rationale: This is the industrial-organization analogue of a practical mechanism: estimate primitives, simulate counterfactual allocations, and evaluate policy. The contribution is both technically deep and institutionally useful for antitrust and regulation.

nominations.contribution: for the theory of two-sided markets and platform competition

people.name: Jean-Charles Rochet
people.affiliation: University of Geneva and Toulouse School of Economics

key_works: Rochet and Tirole, 2003: Platform Competition in Two-Sided Markets, Journal of the European Economic Association
Armstrong, 2006: Competition in Two-Sided Markets, RAND Journal of Economics
Rochet and Tirole, 2006: Two-Sided Markets: A Progress Report, RAND Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The work identifies why ordinary one-sided price logic fails when participation externalities are central. Its importance is enhanced by direct relevance to payment systems, digital platforms and market-design questions about access rules.

nominations.contribution: for measuring firm dynamics, job flows and productivity reallocation

people.name: Steven J. Davis
people.affiliation: University of Chicago Booth School of Business

people.name: John Van Reenen
people.affiliation: London School of Economics and Massachusetts Institute of Technology

key_works: Davis and Haltiwanger, 1992: Gross Job Creation, Gross Job Destruction, and Employment Reallocation, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Davis, Haltiwanger and Schuh, 1996: Job Creation and Destruction, MIT Press
Bloom and Van Reenen, 2007: Measuring and Explaining Management Practices across Firms and Countries, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: This work made firm heterogeneity and reallocation measurable at scale. It is not a theorem-driven contribution, but it changed the empirical constraints that any serious theory of firms and productivity must satisfy.

nominations.contribution: for the empirical analysis of markups, pass-through and market power in production
key_works: De Loecker and Warzynski, 2012: Markups and Firm-Level Export Status, American Economic Review
De Loecker, Eeckhout and Unger, 2020: The Rise of Market Power and the Macroeconomic Implications, Quarterly Journal of Economics
Goldberg, Khandelwal, Pavcnik and Topalova, 2010: Imported Intermediate Inputs and Domestic Product Growth: Evidence from India, Quarterly Journal of Economics
nominations.rationale: The contribution put market power and pass-through back into the quantitative center of IO and macro-industrial analysis. I would seek reassurance on identification and robustness, but the policy importance is large.

nominations.contribution: for the economic analysis of vertical restraints, exclusion and antitrust policy
key_works: Joskow, 1985: Vertical Integration and Long-Term Contracts: The Case of Coal-Burning Electric Generating Plants, Journal of Law, Economics, and Organization
Rey and Tirole, 2007: A Primer on Foreclosure, in Handbook of Industrial Organization
Whinston, 2006: Lectures on Antitrust Economics, MIT Press
nominations.rationale: This line clarifies when private contracting arrangements are efficiency-enhancing and when they exclude rivals. Its relevance is strongest where legal remedies must be translated into implementable market rules.
